summary:
Baden-Württemberg stands under Germany's national framework. Federal constitutional and equality protections apply nationwide, identity documents and marriage law are uniform across the Länder, and no Land can remove that federal floor.

Custody placement is the sharpest documented exposure for a trans visitor. German prisons operate under statutory separation with a binary men and women housing model, and placement corresponding to a prisoner's gender identity has been practised only in exceptional cases. The Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony gives that reading of § 170(2) of the Lower Saxony correctional act as the operating rule and runs a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison.

Baden-Württemberg's own prison law retains the unrevised 1970s-era placement rules, and the Verfassungsblog analysis of 18 March 2026 does not name the Land among those with updated provisions. A majority of the German Länder now operate revised rules: a new Art. 17 of Rhineland-Palatinate's prison law has been in force since 1 March 2026, and Bavarian, Saxon and Hamburg provisions have also recently entered into force. Only Bremen's law explicitly references the registered gender entry, while other Länder do so implicitly.

How the exception is applied in practice remains unsettled. In August 2025 the chief prosecutor for Halle stated that Marla-Svenja Liebich, whose gender entry was changed to female at the end of 2024 under the Self-Determination Act, would serve an 18-month sentence for incitement at Chemnitz women's prison with placement reviewed at intake. After her extradition from Czechia in July 2026 she was transferred to a men's prison despite being legally registered as a woman since 2025; authorities cited the safety of prisoners at the women's facility, and critics called the gender change an abuse of the self-determination law. The transfer indicates that placement follows the civil-registry entry and that exceptions permitting placement contrary to that entry are invoked inconsistently.

DW reported on 23 August 2023 that German prisons offer few safe spaces for trans inmates, a finding illustrated by the case of climate activist Penelope Frank of Last Generation, legally recorded male, who faced assignment to a men's prison if convicted.

Screening is a documented flashpoint. In June 2025 the DJ and producer BASHKKA filed a legal complaint under Germany's Equal Treatment Act over a screening at Frankfurt Airport on 23 November 2024, in which officers allegedly deliberately disregarded her gender identity. She characterised the incident as a targeted, degrading act of transphobic harassment and gave Resident Advisor a copy of her statement to the airport.

Access to women-protected facilities has been contested since the Self-Determination Act took effect on 1 January 2025. A Deutscher Sauna-Bund guideline issued in January 2025 restricting women's saunas to persons whose primary sex characteristics correspond set off a debate about registered trans women's access, in which trans woman Alessia Dorigo argued that claiming a trans identity on a whim is unrealistic.

Reporting and support machinery exists for hostility encountered in country. The STOP the HATE campaign site, run by the Prevention and Empowerment organisation in northern Germany, provides a counselling finder sorted by topic, emergency guidance including an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base covering underreporting, evidence preservation, witness support and reporting channels.
tangentialFactors:
Prison placement rules in most Länder have stood unchanged since the 1970s and are now being revised, so a trans visitor's custody exposure depends on which Land holds them. Baden-Württemberg sits on the unrevised side of that divide while a majority of Länder have moved, and the Verfassungsblog analysis argues there is no constitutional duty to anchor placement to the registered gender entry, contending instead that a prisoner's own self-declaration would intrude less on the right to gender self-determination.

Tagesspiegel Queerspiegel reported on how Berlin saunas and similar venues now treat trans women, after months of public argument over women-protected spaces and fears that the self-declaration route would be misused. The Deutscher Sauna-Bund guideline of January 2025 and the position taken by Alessia Dorigo belong to that same national argument rather than to any Baden-Württemberg rule.

The Berlin prison service maintains an official page in German with information and contacts for trans, inter and non-binary persons held across the city's facilities. No equivalent official Land-level page for Baden-Württemberg appears in the sources.
localsOnly:
Gender entry changes run through the Self-Determination Act, in force since 1 January 2025 on a self-declaration route; Marla-Svenja Liebich's entry was changed to female at the end of 2024 under that law, and she was recorded as a woman from 2025. Marriage and identity document rules are uniform nationwide, so a resident of Baden-Württemberg uses the same procedure as anywhere in Germany.

The STOP the HATE campaign site, run by the Prevention and Empowerment organisation in northern Germany, maintains a counselling finder sorted by topic, emergency guidance with an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base addressing underreporting, how to preserve evidence, support for witnesses and the available reporting channels.

The Berlin prison service's official German-language page carries information and contacts for trans, inter and non-binary detainees in that city's facilities, and the Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony continues a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Baden-Württemberg has a pending amendment to its prison law is unresolved in the sources; the Verfassungsblog analysis of 18 March 2026 simply does not name the Land among those with revised placement rules, and the text of the Baden-Württemberg provision itself was not available here.

The claim that other Länder reference the registered gender entry only implicitly is the Verfassungsblog author's characterisation and was not checked against the individual statutes.

The outcome of BASHKKA's Equal Treatment Act complaint over the Frankfurt Airport screening of 23 November 2024 is unresolved; the sources record the filing in June 2025 and her account of the incident, not any decision.

Whether the July 2026 transfer of Marla-Svenja Liebich to a men's prison reflects a settled rule or an exceptional, politically pressured decision is not settled in the sources, and intake practice in Baden-Württemberg prisons specifically is not sourced.
